  • India could overtake China in affluent consumers by 2036: Report reveals how 8.2 crore more Indians could enter the high-spending consumer class

    India's affluent consumer population is set to exceed China's by 2036, a shift that could significantly reshape global spending patterns over the next decade. The United States is still expected to have the world's largest affluent consumer base. Companies will need to offer both value-driven and premium products to meet the evolving needs of consumers. This changing market will require a strategic approach to product development and pricing.<br />

    India eyes 14-fold jump in electronic component production by FY31: Report

    India aims for USD 500 billion in electronics production by FY31. Electronic component production is projected to reach USD 150 billion, a significant increase. Mobile phone manufacturing will also grow substantially, reaching USD 159 billion by FY31. Other categories like consumer electronics and IT hardware will see considerable expansion. This growth signifies India's expanding electronics manufacturing capabilities across diverse products.

    UPI completes 10 years, clocks nearly 13,000-fold rise in transaction volume

    UPI has completed a decade of transforming India’s digital payments ecosystem, with annual transactions surging from 1.78 crore in 2016-17 to 24,162 crore in 2025-26. Transaction value rose to Rs 314 lakh crore, while monthly volumes hit a record 2,366 crore in July 2026. UPI now operates across 11 countries and accounts for nearly 49% of global real-time payments.

    Before Xi Jinping's likely India visit, Chinese money is pouring in

    India is cautiously reopening economic channels with China as Chinese linked investment returns after years of restrictions following the Galwan clash. More than $500 million has entered under revised investment rules, while NSA Ajit Doval’s Beijing visit and Xi Jinping’s expected India visit signal improving diplomatic ties. India is balancing economic cooperation with national security safeguards and strategic scrutiny.

    More cars, thinner margins: Why rising sales aren’t boosting automakers’ profits

    Indian car makers see strong sales volumes, but profits are declining. Rising commodity prices and currency shifts are impacting manufacturer margins. Maruti Suzuki's profits fell despite record sales, showing margin erosion. Tata Motors and Hyundai also reported lower profits due to cost pressures. Automakers are investing heavily in new technologies and plants, affecting current earnings.

    IndiGo co-founder Gangwal commits Rs 300 cr more to IIT Kanpur medical sciences school

    Rakesh Gangwal has committed an additional Rs 300 crore to IIT Kanpur's medical school. This significant funding follows his previous Rs 100 crore contribution in 2022. The institute plans to establish a super-speciality hospital and a cancer research centre on campus. These facilities will foster interdisciplinary collaboration between engineers and medical professionals. The Gangwal School aims to advance medical education and healthcare innovation across India.

    India’s new capex cycle is being driven by cash-rich giants, HSBC India CEO says

    India's corporate investment cycle now features financially stronger companies expanding capacity. These well-capitalized groups are using internal cash flows for growth and consolidation. This differs from the earlier debt-heavy boom which relied on bank financing. HSBC India's balance sheet is expanding significantly, crossing five lakh crore rupees. Global capital flows require fresh triggers like reforms or FDI announcements.

Singapore wants to pay parents over $55,000 per child to boost birth rate

Singapore will provide nearly S$70,000 (US$55,153) in direct support for every citizen child up to age 17 as it tackles a record-low fertility rate of 0.87. The package includes child credits, grants, childcare subsidies, parental leave and housing support.
